cause: Scroll suspension removed the animation src and replaced the keyed image with the static thumbnail, restarting the native decoder on resume.
implemented: Retain only already-started lightweight animation images until foreground loss or virtual component unmount. Scroll and brief viewport exit use visibility:hidden with a static thumbnail overlay. New visible cards wait until scrolling is idle.
browser_semantics: Chrome's animation clock advances while the retained image is hidden; the result preserves its timeline and does not provide exact frame pause/resume.

resource_boundary.ownership: One retained preview per mounted GalleryCardImage; no cross-component or full-library cache.
resource_boundary.virtual_window: GalleryView.vue uses getVirtualItems with overscan:2 and mounts cards only from those rows; unmount clears animation src.
resource_boundary.media: Existing production lightweight motion derivative remains unchanged; no original GIF fallback or new decoding player.

verification.gif_browser: 12 checks passed at 1440/390/320px: scroll continuity, mounted brief exit/return, defer newly visible playback, release on background/unmount.
verification.webp_browser: Same 12 checks passed; normal animation/static/masked-thumbnail states additionally assert no placeholder. Final before/resume/return screenshots retained.
verification.cpu: Short AB/BA on 16 synthetic 360x270 GIFs, one second per mode: hidden CPU 0/0 seconds and Decode Image 0/0; static release CPU 0/0.016 and Decode Image 0/0. Visible initial decode count136. Raw results in gallery-paint-cpu.json.

limits: Synthetic native Chrome source component verification only. Solid-color short CPU probe is not user-device performance acceptance. Simulated document background is not a physical phone background test. No EXE verification or playback position preservation across virtual unmount/navigation.
